name: Boor
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog refs for Boor are wordlists only; Roberts 2021 pp.135-136 is subclassification, not description

sources.note: No descriptive references beyond Roberts 2021 (subclassification comment pp. 135–136), Connell 2007, Ethnologue, Moseley 2010; alternative names Bwara, Damraw.
No Boor publication or data listed (only Laal, Fanya, Khoisan, Kanak work).
Nothing on phonology; notes Boor was documented (recordings) by Florian Lionnet, Sandrine Loncke and Remadji Hoinathy in 2012; links to Ethnologue, ELP, Glottolog.

sources.citation: Roberts, James. 2021. Initial findings on the Boor language. Afrika und Übersee 94: 127–140. DOI 10.15460/auue.2021.94.1.242 (CC BY 4.0, Hamburg University Press)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. §3.1 Phonology (pp. 131–133) gives preliminary consonant and vowel charts, remarks on length, nasality and an [ɔ]~[u̯a] alternation; the words stress/accent do not occur anywhere in the article. On tone (p. 133) it says only that the author and Lionnet made impressionistic, incomplete tone markings which are not presented, and that little can be stated about tone before a systematic study.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann & Carsten Peust. 2019. Notes on Gàlì (Miltu), a moribund Chadic language (Republic of Chad). Folia Orientalia 56: 219–230. DOI 10.24425/for.2019.130711
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not about Boor: describes Miltu (Gali), with a tone section (three levels, two contours) for Miltu only; Boor appears once, as the language of Damraw, 'possibly a dialect of Gali (Miltu)'. No Boor data, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Lionnet, Florian. 2012. Notes de terrain Boor, carnets 5 et 6. Ms. (field notebooks; a few hundred words, sentences, pronouns, verb paradigms, impressionistic tone marks)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The most extensive primary data on Boor in existence (per Roberts 2021: 128); unpublished, but any future prosodic statement will come from these notes or Lionnet's 2012 recordings.

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce. 2007. Endangered languages in Central Africa. In M. Brenzinger (ed.), Language Diversity Endangered, 163–178. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.

sources.note: Glottolog's only other reference; an endangerment overview that will not contain a stress statement, listed for completeness.
